# Ontario Freelance Designer Contract Risk Snapshot

For a 12-month freelance design contract starting **2026-03-15**, the biggest review points are the **non-compete**, **termination notice**, **IP ownership**, and **net 45 payment timing**. The list below is a practical risk check, not a legal opinion.

## Contract Clauses to Review Before Signing

| Clause | Main issue | Why it matters | Negotiation point |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-compete | May restrict future work after the contract ends | Could limit your ability to take similar clients or projects | Narrow the scope, shorten the duration, or remove it entirely |
| 30-day termination notice | Either side may end the deal with 30 days’ notice | You may lose expected income or be left with unfinished work | Add a minimum commitment, termination fee, or payment for work in progress |
| Ownership of all deliverables by client | Client may want broad ownership of all work product | Could transfer more rights than intended, including drafts, concepts, or reusable components | Limit assignment to final paid deliverables only; keep pre-existing tools and templates |
| Payment net 45 | Payment arrives 45 days after invoice | Cash flow delay, especially for a freelancer | Ask for net 15 or net 30, deposits, or milestone billing |
| Scope of work | Contract may be vague on what is included | Scope creep can increase unpaid work | Define deliverables, revision rounds, and out-of-scope rates |
| Independent contractor status | The agreement may not match the real working relationship | Can affect taxes, control, and liability expectations | Ensure the contract reflects freelance status and your own tools/processes |
| Confidentiality and portfolio use | May limit how you can show the work | Could prevent portfolio or case-study use | Ask for permission to display non-confidential work after launch |
| Liability and indemnity | You may be exposed to broad risk | One-sided clauses can make you responsible for more than your fee | Cap liability to fees paid under the contract |

## Negotiation Points That Usually Matter Most

- **Non-compete:** Ask whether it can be removed, or replaced with a narrower **non-solicit** or confidentiality clause.
- **Termination:** Request payment for completed work, partial milestones, and a clear handoff process if the startup ends the agreement early.
- **Ownership:** Clarify that the client owns only the **final deliverables paid for in full**, while you keep your **pre-existing methods, templates, fonts/licenses, and reusable design systems**.
- **Payment:** Push for **net 15 or net 30**, plus a deposit or milestone payments for a 12-month engagement.
- **Revisions and scope:** Set a fixed number of revision rounds and a written change-order process.
- **Portfolio rights:** Ask for the right to show selected work in your portfolio after public release, subject to confidentiality.

## Plain-Language Questions to Ask Before Signing

- What exactly counts as a **deliverable** under this contract?
- Does the **non-compete** stop me from working with any similar startup, or only direct competitors?
- How long does the non-compete last, and what geographic area does it cover?
- If the startup ends the contract with 30 days’ notice, do I get paid for work already done and approved?
- Can we change payment terms from **net 45** to **net 30** or include milestone payments?
- Is a deposit possible at the start of the contract?
- Do I keep ownership of my **templates, design systems, source files, and reusable assets**?
- Does “ownership of all deliverables” include drafts, concepts, and unused options?
- Can I use the finished work in my portfolio after launch?
- How many revision rounds are included before extra fees apply?
- Who approves work, and what happens if feedback is delayed?
- Are there any indemnity or liability clauses that could make me responsible for more than my fee?
- Is the contract meant to make me an independent contractor, not an employee?
